en.headline: Hong Kong takes first Asian Games esports medal of these Games
en.dek: Lee Yin-hei, Wong Yuk-cheung and Yip Man-ho won bronze in the mixed martial-arts team event after beating Thailand and falling to Japan.
body: Hong Kong, China claimed bronze in the Asian Games esports mixed martial-arts team event on Friday in Nagoya, the delegation’s first medal of these Games in esports.

Lee Yin-hei, Wong Yuk-cheung and Yip Man-ho competed across Street Fighter 6, Tekken 8 and The King of Fighters XV. After the group stage they beat Thailand 3-2 in the quarter-finals and then lost 0-3 to host Japan in the semi-finals. The event has no bronze-medal match, so a semi-final place secured third.

Local reports said the result is Hong Kong’s second successive Asian Games medal in esports. Under the Hong Kong Jockey Club Elite Athletes Incentive Awards Scheme, the three players stand to share a cash award of 500,000 dollars.

zh.headline: 港隊亞運電競綜合格鬥摘銅 今屆電競開齋
zh.dek: 李衍熙、黃育祥及葉文豪周五在名古屋擊敗泰國後四強不敵日本，賽事不設銅牌戰，港隊穩奪季軍。
body: 港隊周五在名古屋亞運電子競技綜合格鬥團體賽奪得銅牌，成為代表團本屆賽事首面電競獎牌。
李衍熙、黃育祥及葉文豪出戰《街頭霸王6》、《鐵拳8》及《拳皇XV》。分組賽後，三人在八強以3：2擊敗泰國，四強以0：3不敵東道主日本。項目不設季軍戰，晉級四強即鎖定銅牌。
本地報道指，港隊連續兩屆亞運在電競項目上牌。按香港賽馬會優秀運動員獎勵計劃，三人合共可獲50萬元現金獎勵。
